questions.title: Ventral as the synonym of anterior
questions.question: Which anatomical term has the exact same positional meaning as the word anterior?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Inferior means toward the feet, describing the vertical axis, not the front-back axis that anterior describes.
explanations.B: Correct. Ventral is synonymous with anterior — both describe the front, or belly-side, surface or direction of the body in the standard anatomical position. This is the opposite of dorsal (posterior, the back surface), and distinct from superior/inferior, which describe the vertical axis rather than the front-back axis.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Superior means toward the head, describing the vertical axis, not the front-back axis that anterior describes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dorsal means posterior (the back surface), the exact opposite of anterior, not its synonym.

questions.title: Bilateral: both sides of the body
questions.question: Which anatomical term is specifically related to both right and left sides of the body?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Ipsilateral means the same side as a stated reference point, not both sides together.
explanations.B: Correct. Bilateral is the anatomical term describing a structure, finding or process that relates to both the right and left sides of the body together. This is distinct from unilateral (one side only), ipsilateral (the same side as a reference point) and contralateral (the opposite side from a reference point).
explanations.C: Incorrect. Contralateral means the opposite side from a stated reference point, not both sides together.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Unilateral means one side only, the opposite of bilateral's both-sides meaning.

questions.title: Synergist: assisting the prime mover
questions.question: What is the muscle called that assists the prime mover to produce a specific movement?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The antagonist opposes the prime mover, producing the opposite movement, rather than assisting it.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The fixator stabilises the muscle's bony origin so the prime mover can act efficiently; it does not itself assist the movement's direction.
explanations.C: Correct. A synergist is a muscle that assists the prime mover (agonist) in producing a specific movement, either by adding force in the same direction or by preventing unwanted secondary movements. This is one of four standard muscle-action roles taught together with the agonist (prime mover), antagonist (opposes) and fixator (stabilises the origin).
explanations.D: Incorrect. The agonist (prime mover) is the muscle chiefly responsible for the movement itself, not the muscle that merely assists it.

questions.title: White matter is formed by nerve fibers
questions.question: Which of the following structural components forms the white matter in the nervous system?

explanations.A: Incorrect. Nerve cell bodies form grey matter, not white matter.
explanations.B: Correct. White matter in the nervous system is formed by nerve fibers (axons), most of them myelinated — the myelin sheath's lipid content is what gives white matter its pale colour. This is distinct from grey matter, which is formed by nerve cell bodies, and from synaptic vesicles and dendritic trees, neither of which is the structural component that defines white matter as a tissue region.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Synaptic vesicles are small membrane-bound sacs of neurotransmitter inside a nerve terminal, not the structural component that defines white matter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Dendritic trees are the branching receptive processes of a single neuron, found within grey matter regions, not the component that defines white matter.

questions.title: Medulla oblongata as a core part of the brainstem
questions.question: Which of the following structures is considered a core part of the brainstem?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The cerebral cortex is the cerebrum's outer grey-matter layer, a distinct structure from the brainstem.
explanations.B: Correct. The medulla oblongata is a core part of the brainstem, the stalk-like lower part of the brain that connects the spinal cord to the rest of the brain and houses the vital cardiorespiratory centres. The brainstem's other core parts are the pons and midbrain, distinguishing it from the cerebral cortex, cerebellar hemispheres and corpus callosum.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The cerebellar hemispheres are paired lobes of the cerebellum, attached to the brainstem by the cerebellar peduncles but anatomically and developmentally distinct from it.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The corpus callosum is the white-matter tract connecting the two cerebral hemispheres, a distinct structure from the brainstem.

questions.title: The free morula's time in the uterine cavity
questions.question: The developing morula remains completely free in the uterine cavity for how many days before changing into a blastocyst?

explanations.A: Correct. Per this FOMSCU source's own teaching timetable, the developing morula remains free (unattached) within the uterine cavity for about three days before it transforms into a blastocyst, ahead of implantation. The morula is a solid ball of blastomeres produced by cleavage of the fertilised zygote, with no internal cavity of its own. The fluid-filled cavity (blastocele) that defines the blastocyst stage only forms after this free period in the uterine cavity, per this source's teaching.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Seven days is too long an interval for the free-morula period in this source's own teaching timetable.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Almost twenty-four days is far too long an interval, well past the first week of development during which this transition occurs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Sixteen continuous days is far too long an interval, well past the first week of development during which this transition occurs.
